study.question: Can auxiliary feedback losses improve a shared context-conditioned history query, or should they only read a query learned by click? The observed limitation is that the best context-event router has independent per-task projection matrices: it exploits task/context interactions but auxiliary supervision cannot train the click matrix.
study.hypothesis: Provisional directional prediction: replacing four independent context-to-event matrices by the click-anchored matrix shared across all task routes can let rare-feedback supervision regularize a common history query. Shared/joint should improve click validation AUC over shared/primary if that auxiliary supervision is useful. Earlier negative sharing/transfer evidence makes harm plausible; the mechanistic claim is limited to this newly supported context-conditioned path. No claim of originality or general auxiliary benefit.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary section4.3 inspected. Inherit target-conditioned unnormalized local activation; this proposal ties only the separately added context-event query and compares its training ownership. It is neither a DIN reproduction nor a new-attention priority claim.

Pinned benchmark code inspected at lines25-115 and204-313 (git90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d; text SHA e3750a73af1ceb6b2be4bf9355b70a9ad356985a3c465ef27238ef7e0f28fb4c). It contains shared/specific task tokens, hub aggregation and affine broadcasts. Here one existing zero-initialized context-to-feedback/match projection is tied across tasks, with an auxiliary derivative control; no hub stack, SDPA, token updates or benchmark code copied. Original INFNet paper detailed text is unavailable, so stronger novelty remains unverified.

Earlier input-only position-route sharing hurt click relative to primary-owned/task-private controls. Current intervention concerns the empirically stronger learned context-to-event query, not the input-only positional matrix. The prior negative is a caution and alternative explanation, not evidence that this new adaptation works.

study.proposed_difference: Add architecture switches context_projection_sharing={task,shared} and context_projection_aux_gradient={joint,primary}. In shared mode every task reads the matrix at labels.index(is_click), never a hard-coded task index. In primary mode detach only the selected matrix for auxiliary task computations; the contextual input remains detached for auxiliaries as in the incumbent. No output or probability is detached. Private/joint is the exact parent function for arbitrary parameter values. All variants are standalone and retain all allocated matrices; unused shared-mode rows remain zero from their zero initialization. Three runs: shared/joint candidate, shared/primary backward control, and task/joint parent reproduction. This is a simple supervision contrast plus a closest architectural replacement control, not a full factorial.
predictions: P1 (primary): shared/joint click AUC should exceed shared/primary; a difference below0.0002 AUC is practically unresolved at this exploratory single seed and must not be selected as mechanism support. If neither beats the parent, retain the parent for quality even if the internal contrast is positive.

P2: Shared/joint and shared/primary have identical forward probabilities at the same arbitrary parameter state. Per-task auxiliary losses have nonzero new-path derivatives into the click matrix only in joint; click new-path derivatives agree. All task-specific prediction towers and other inherited auxiliary paths keep learning.

P3: Task/joint reproduces the parent initialization, full fixed-state forward and gradients, parameter count56423003 (embedding56054432, dense368571), and approximately its0.6672676914 click AUC under the identical deterministic recipe. Investigate discrepancies; do not reinterpret them as a scientific effect.

P4: Evaluate all four task AUC/logloss, auxiliary mean AUC separately, total parameters, train/allocated GPU/wall seconds, examples, memory, inference throughput and whole-batch p50/p95 latency. Sharing retains56423003 allocated parameters; active context entries fall from15360 to3840 for inherited C=192. Do not claim efficiency from allocation alone.

P5: Use pre-existing history bins empty,1..16,17..64,>64 and report samples/positives/negatives. Route-path differences should chiefly appear in nonempty histories; empty-history predictions can still differ after training via shared parameters. Additional unsupported slices are exploratory and cannot be invented from unavailable inputs.
falsifiers: Shared/joint at or below shared/primary weakens or rejects useful auxiliary supervision for this implementation/seed; shared/primary matching or beating joint favors read-only auxiliary use. A small difference remains unresolved.
Both shared variants below reproduced task/private parent support task-specific context queries over this tying scheme; they do not refute all possible cross-task modeling.

Any fixed-state forward mismatch between shared joint/primary, unexpected gradient leakage, parent-control mismatch, padding/current-action dependence, nonfinite loss/gradients or resource-cap overrun invalidates execution before predictive interpretation.
An improvement only over the private parent without an advantage over shared/primary supports query tying/regularization, not useful auxiliary training of the shared query.
A later matched-gradient-scale control or paired seeds erasing the difference would weaken semantic-complementarity or repeated-effect explanations.
